diagnosis.root_cause: Two active CRM records are assigned to the same physical ONU slot EPON0/4:17, with different ONU line IDs. Only one ONU can occupy that slot, creating a provisioning and identity conflict even though the currently observed ONU is online.
evidence: The CRM view explicitly lists two different active line IDs on EPON0/4:17 and reports a duplicate ONU slot conflict.
The target ONU is currently online and responding, so this is not an ONU-offline or PON outage fault.
RX power is normal at approximately -20.9 dBm, TX power is normal at approximately +2.4 dBm, and the seven-day optical readings are stable.
TX bias current is stable and healthy, distance is constant at 134, and there is no evidence of fibre, laser, or distance degradation.
Other ONUs on EPON0/4 are online with normal optical readings, while all eight OLT PONs are healthy; therefore there is no shared PON, splitter, port, or OLT failure.
The router heartbeat, OLT CPU, memory, temperature, VLAN 1044, RADIUS entry, and CRM/RADIUS identity mapping are all healthy.
The customer has only two sessions in the last 24 hours with long durations, so the data does not support session flapping.
The conflict involves two customer records on one slot, so the affected scope is multi-customer even though the physical location is limited to EPON0/4:17.

remediation.action: Reconcile the two CRM records against the ONU MAC and field installation at EPON0/4:17. Remove or correct the stale record, or move the valid subscriber to the correct free slot, then reprovision the ONU and verify its line ID, MAC, RADIUS mapping, online state, and service traffic.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two active CRM records place different ONU MACs on EPON0/4:17. A slot holds exactly one ONU, so one record is stale. The live probe returns a single device, and its MAC matches the subject record, identifying the other as the leftover.
expected_reasoning: The CRM view lists two active customers on EPON0/4:17 with different ONU MACs
A PON slot holds exactly one ONU, so this state is physically impossible
The live probe of that slot returns a single responding device
The probe's optical values match the subject record's cached reading of -20.88 dBm
RADIUS holds a consistent entry for the subject with normal sessions and traffic
The second record therefore does not correspond to an installed device and is stale
The optical layer is healthy and neither customer is experiencing a service fault
This is a record defect of the same class as the 644 such interfaces in the estate

expected_escalation.review_reason: One of two CRM records on this slot is stale; deleting the wrong one disconnects a live customer

distractors: Nothing is failing and no customer has complained
Both records are marked active and look equally legitimate in CRM
